pages.text: It was a very windy day. Pipo's yellow scarf slipped off and flew away.
It was his only scarf, knitted by Mom. "I will catch it!" Pipo ran after it.
Grandpa, Mrs. Goose, and Mr. Horse joined in. Mr. Horse raised his arms. "Catch it!"
The scarf fluttered over the hill. Mr. Horse ran first.
Mrs. Goose flapped into the air. Grandpa followed, waving his stick.
All three jumped at once. Crash! They collided and rolled about.
The scarf was gone from sight. The three lay tangled in the grass, blinking.
Pipo stopped quietly. The wind pressed his ears flat—it was blowing toward the flock.
Yellow fluttered among the sheep. One sheep wore the scarf around its neck.
When Pipo called, the sheep ambled over. He took back the scarf and wrapped it tightly. The three grown-ups were still tangled on the grass.
